I saved the 3Q answers to `/work/answer.json`. Running the same code on 2Q gives all 10 reference values exactly.

| Item | 3Q answer |
|---|---|
| a | consumer, 287,348,307 |
| b | 244 |
| c | svc, 267,144,376 |
| d | 2025-07 |
| e | u104@ex.com |
| f | 229 |
| g | 683,980 |
| h | -11.7 (September vs. August) |

The data needed four adjustments before the 2Q check would match:
- **Time zone:** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC. Only converting it to Korean time (+9 hours) before splitting into quarters and months reproduced the 2Q values. Without the shift, every figure except the top category, the top month and the email was off.
- **Segment names:** The same segment was written in different ways, with stray spaces and mixed upper/lower case (e.g. " consumer", "Enterprise "). I trimmed and lowercased them.
- **Duplicate customers:** One email can have several customer records, sometimes with different segments. For b and f, I counted each lowercased, trimmed email as one customer. For a, I used the segment on the record each order belongs to.
- **Refunds:** All refund rows matched an order line, and no refund quantity was larger than the quantity ordered.

STATUS: DONE
